evidence.title: SOP-07 - purpose of the main steps (QA note)
evidence.claim: The first acetone rinse is used to remove the product film before the next batch (2016).
evidence.quote: The first acetone rinse removes the product film before the next batch.

evidence.title: SOP-07 Solvent cleaning of dispersers and mixing vessels
evidence.claim: The first rinse step (40 L acetone, 10 min) was still in effect in September 2014.
evidence.quote: Rinse with 40 L acetone, circulate 10 min, drain to waste solvent.

evidence.title: CHANGE REQUEST CR-1998-009
evidence.claim: In 1998, it was noted that acetone alone cannot dissolve residues from chlorinated rubber paints (CR-55 line), requiring a subsequent xylene wipe.
evidence.quote: residues of the chlorinated rubber paints (CR-55 line) are not dissolved by acetone and contaminate the next batch

evidence.title: Product portfolio memo PM-2009-002
evidence.claim: The chlorinated rubber range (CR-55), which required additional cleaning beyond acetone, was discontinued in 2009.
evidence.quote: The chlorinated rubber range (CR-55 swimming-pool and road-marking paints) is discontinued

evidence.claim: Residual acetone in D-2 caused defects in AF-12 lot 15-0412 when charged hot in 2015.

verdict.process_name: SOP-07 solvent cleaning of dispersers and mixing vessels
verdict.instruction: First rinse: circulate 40 L acetone (RM-301) for 10 min; drain to waste solvent.
verdict.reason: The first acetone rinse is used to remove product film before the next batch (E6). This function is essential for the current cleaning process of dispersers and mixing vessels (E1).

chain.claim: The first acetone rinse removes the product film before the next batch

counter_evidence.claim: Residual acetone caused popping and craters in AF-12 lot 15-0412
counter_evidence.resolution: This is a failure of the subsequent drying/removal process, not a reason to remove the initial cleaning rinse.
